text:
Jordan (support): Hey team — incoming from a paying customer (BrightApps). Their project-level quota tile shows ~750 requests remaining for the rolling window but they're getting 429s from the API. Ticket#: #92514. Repro steps and headers below.

Jordan (support): Repro (from customer's project key):
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-xxxx" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
Response headers from a failing request we got: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2025 14:05:03 GMT
x-rw-ratelimit-limit: 30000
x-rw-ratelimit-remaining: 742
x-rw-ratelimit-reset: 1691889300
x-rw-request-id: r-0a1b2c3d
```
Note: dashboard shows remaining=742 in project tile (same number) but request was rejected. Customer says this happens intermittently for several projects under their org.

Maya (eng-sre): Thanks Jordan. Two quick asks: 1) can we get the raw request IDs and timestamps where they got 429s? 2) are they on Dedicated or Hosted?

Jordan (support): Sending sample request ids in the ticket — r-0a1b2c3d, r-0d4e5f6g, r-0h7i8j9k. They are on Hosted (standard tier).

Samir (infra): Quick theory: dashboard tiles use aggregated metering from the billing pipeline (5s rollup TTL), enforcement uses Redis counters with a short TTL and different window math. If there's a scrubbing job or late ingestion, tile could be stale. But header shows remaining=742 which matches tile — that suggests enforcement and tile read from same source? weird.

Maya (eng-sre): Can we pull the enforcement logs for r-0a1b2c3d from the rate-limiter cluster for that minute? I want to check which token bucket rejected it and value at decision time.

Samir (infra): Pulling now. Paste from limiter logs (redacted):
```
[2025-08-12T14:05:02.943Z] request_id=r-0a1b2c3d project=brightapps-prod project_quota=30000 window=3600 decision=reject remaining=0 backend_counter_ts=1691889248
```
So enforcement saw remaining=0 for the bucket at enforcement time. That contradicts x-rw-ratelimit-remaining header the API returned. Means header construction might be pulled from a different cache (stale) or rate-limiter is using different aggregation (per-project vs per-org).

Ana M (product): Could this be an org-level shared pool being consumed first? The dashboard tile is per-project, but enforcement could deduct from org pool and the header shows project remaining, not effective remaining.

Maya (eng-sre): Good point. Jordan: does the customer have org-wide traffic coming from other projects? They mentioned spikes from ingestion workers.

Jordan (support): Yes — they confirmed several background projects throttle-batch-* that spike hourly. They said project A (the one in ticket) is the one showing 742 on the UI.

Samir (infra): I looked at the enforcement policy code — if org_fallback is enabled and org pool is exhausted, we mark requests as rejected but headers still call get_project_remaining() which reads the project counter only. So header can be misleading. That would explain enforcement remaining=0 but header=742. 

Maya (eng-sre): So race between org consumption and project-level counters. We should consider either: a) include effective_remaining header (min(project, org)) or b) ensure enforcement uses same counter the header reads.

Ana M (product): Product decision: customers expect tile to reflect enforceable capacity. Dashboard and headers should be consistent with enforcement semantics. Proposed short-term: change header to include both project_remaining and effective_remaining. Long-term: align metering reads.

Chris O (ops): Operationally, we should also check the metrics pipeline for delayed updates — but logs show enforcement-only rejection so pipeline delay not root cause here. Looks like fallback semantics.

Jordan (support): Customer asks for an explanation and a mitigation. Can we temporarily lift org fallback for BrightApps while we patch? Or give them an org-level bump?

Samir (infra): We can whitelist their org for 24h by disabling org_fallback flag for their org in control plane. That will route enforcement to project-only counters. Temporary mitigation: whitelist id=org-8732 for 2 hours.

Maya (eng-sre): I'll prepare a small patch to return both headers. Patch: add x-rw-effective-remaining and keep the old x-rw-ratelimit-remaining (backcompat). Also add a note in docs. I'll open PR and request urgent review.

Ana M (product): Please also add a line to the dashboard tooltip: "Tile shows project remaining; enforcement may apply org-level pools. See docs for effective limits."

Jordan (support): I'll update the customer: tell them root cause is org fallback semantics causing enforcement-visible remaining to be lower than project tile/headers. Offer 24h whitelist and a credit for the failed requests while we patch. They accepted the 24h whitelist.

Maya (eng-sre): PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/rate-limiter/pull/812 — includes header changes and tests. Planning deploy to canary tonight.

Samir (infra): Ops action: applying temporary whitelist now. Done. org-8732 flagged until 2025-08-13T14:05:00Z.

Jordan (support): Customer notified and ticket updated with the workaround + ETA for patch. They were appreciative. :thumbsup:

Ana M (product): Follow-up: add to backlog to unify meter/source-of-truth for dashboard/enforcement (P0? maybe P1). Creating ticket in product board.

Maya (eng-sre): Will monitor canary logs for any regressions after deploy. Will post an update here when canary is green.

Jordan (support): Thanks everyone — marking thread for closure after canary success. I'll add a small credit in billing system for the impacted window.

Chris O (ops): Canary deployed to 3 nodes, no errors in first 30m. Reporting back in 1h.

Maya (eng-sre): Canary looks good. Merging and scheduling full rollout at 02:00 UTC.

Jordan (support): Closing loop with customer and closing internal thread.
